# Power to identify differences in proportion
Given $C$ cells per individual, consider a cell type $i$ with proportion $p_i$.  The estimation cell proportion, $\hat{p_i}$, is based on observing $C$ cells, and the sampling variance of this fraction is $p_i(1-p_i)/C$.  Consider two subsets of the data with sample sizes $n_1$ and $n_2$.

Power is based on the size of each of the two subsets, and Cohens d:
$d = \frac{|\mu_1 - \mu_2|}{\sigma}$

where $\sigma^2$ is the pooled variance:

$\sigma^2 = \frac{(n_1-1)s^2_1 + (n_2-1)s^2_2}{n_1+n_2-2}$

I have confirmed these curves with simulations. This assumes no cell type misclassification error.

```{r power.analysis.proportions, fig.height=4, fig.width=12}
n_samples = c(CTL = 200, AD=200)
n_cells = 5000
n_cells_max = 10000
prop_diff = list(c(0.001, 0.002), c(0.0001, 0.0003), c(0.00001, 0.0001))
n_cell_types = 20

getPower = function(n1, n2, p1, p2, C, n_tests){
	sSq1 = p1*(1-p1)/ C
	sSq2 = p2*(1-p2)/ C

	sigSq = ((n1-1)*sSq1 + (n2-1)*sSq2) / (n1 + n2 -2)
	d = abs(p1 - p2)/sqrt(sigSq)

	pwr.t2n.test(n1=n1, n2=n2, d=d, sig.level = 0.05/n_tests )
}

getPowerCurve = function(n1, n2){
	# for each pair of proportions
	lapply(prop_diff, function(prop){
		p1 = prop[1]
		p2 = prop[2]

		# for each cell number
		lapply( seq(10, n_cells_max, by = 3), function(C){
			res = getPower(n1, n2, p1, p2, C, n_cell_types)
			data.frame(n1, n2, p1, p2, C, d = res$d, power= res$power, delta=paste0(p1*100, '% to ', p2*100, '%'))
			}) %>%
		bind_rows
		}) %>%
	bind_rows
}

# for each disease
res = lapply(names(n_samples)[-1], function(ID){
	getPowerCurve(n_samples['CTL'], n_samples[ID])
}) %>%
bind_rows

fig_cell_comp = ggplot(res, aes(C, power, color=delta)) + geom_line(size=1.3) + 
	theme_bw(12) + 
	theme(aspect.ratio=1, plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) + xlab("# of cells") +
	ylim(0, 1) + 
	geom_vline(xintercept=n_cells, color="black", linetype="dashed") + 
	geom_hline(yintercept=0.8, color="red", linetype="dashed") + 
	ylab("Power")
fig_cell_comp
```


Power here is shown applying a Bonferroni correction for testing `r n_cell_types` cell types.

## Get number of cells to get 80% power
```{r, results="asis", echo=FALSE}
# Sample size required to get 80% power
res = data.table(res)
res$Dataset = with(res, paste(delta))
tab = res[,.SD[min(which(power>.80)),],by=Dataset]
tab$Cells_per_individual = as.integer(tab$C)
print(xtable(tab[,c('Dataset', 'Cells_per_individual', 'power')], type="html"), include.rownames=FALSE)
```

# Detectable changes
```{r comp.delta, fig.height=6, cache=TRUE}
n = 200
n1 = n
n2 = n
n_cell_types = 20

res <- 
	lapply(c(1), function(frac){
	lapply(c(.01, .05, .1), function(p1){
		lapply(seq(p1^1.1, p1, length.out=10000), function(p2){
			lapply(c(100, 500, 1000), function(C){
			res = getPower(frac*n1, frac*n2, p1, p2, C, n_cell_types)
			tibble(frac, n1, n2, p1, p2, C, d = res$d, power= res$power)
		}) %>%
		bind_rows
	}) %>%
	bind_rows
}) %>%
bind_rows
}) %>%
bind_rows

res %>%
	ggplot(aes(p1-p2, power, color=factor(C))) +
		geom_line(size=2) +
		theme_bw() +
		theme(aspect.ratio=1) +
		scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0, NA), expand=c(0,0))+	
		scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0, 1.01), expand=c(0,0)) +
		scale_color_discrete("# cells") +
		facet_grid(frac~p1, scales="free_x") +
		xlab("Absulute change in cell fraction") +
		ylab("Power") +
		geom_hline(yintercept=0.8, color="red", linetype="dashed")  

res %>%
	ggplot(aes(p1/p2, power, color=factor(C))) +
		geom_line(size=2) +
		theme_bw() +
		theme(aspect.ratio=1) +
		scale_x_continuous(limits=c(1, 1.2), expand=c(0,0))+	
		scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0, 1.01), expand=c(0,0)) +
		scale_color_discrete("# cells") +
		facet_grid(~p1, scales="free_x") +
		xlab("Relative change in cell fraction") +
		ylab("Power") +
		geom_hline(yintercept=0.8, color="red", linetype="dashed")
```

## Get effect size with 80% power
```{r comp.delta.table, results="asis", echo=FALSE}
tab = res %>%
	group_by(frac, p1, C) %>%
	arrange(pmax(power, 0.8)) %>%
	slice_head(n=1) %>%
	mutate(delta = p1 - p2, FC = p1/p2)

kable(tab, type="html", include.rownames=FALSE)
```




# Differential expression
```{r pow2, fig.height=6}
getPower = function(n1, n2, d, n_tests, rsq){
	# pwr.t2n.test(n1=n1, n2=n2, d=d, sig.level = 0.05/n_tests )

	# Compute n_Eff, need to divide by 2 becaues n is the number in each set
	N_eff = 4 / (1/n1 + 1/n2)
	pwr.t.test(n=N_eff/2 * rsq, d=d, sig.level = 0.05/n_tests )
}

getPowerCurve = function(n1, n2, n_tests, rsq){
	# for each cell number
	res = lapply( seq(0, 2.5, length.out=1000), function(delta){
		res = getPower(n1, n2, delta, n_tests, rsq)
		data.frame(n1, n2, d = res$d, rsq, power= res$power)
		})
	do.call("rbind", res)
}

res = lapply(c(1), function(frac){
	lapply(1:nrow(settings), function(i){

	n_tests = with(settings, nFeatures[i]*n_cell_types[i])
	lapply(names(n_samples)[-1], function(ID){
		lapply( c( .6, .7, .8, .9,1), function(rsq){
			res = getPowerCurve(frac*n_samples['CTL'], frac*n_samples[ID], n_tests, rsq)
			data.frame(Type = settings$Type[i], frac, res)
		}) %>% 
			bind_rows
	}) %>% 
		bind_rows
})%>% 
		bind_rows
})%>% 
		bind_rows

res$rsq_text = with(res, factor(rsq, rev(sort(unique(rsq)))))
res = res[order(res$rsq, decreasing=FALSE),]

res %>%
	mutate(Type = factor(Type,settings$Type)) %>%
	ggplot(aes(d, power, color=rsq_text)) + 
	geom_line(size=1.3) + 
	theme_bw(12) + 
	theme(aspect.ratio=1, plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) + ylim(0, 1) + 
	xlab("Cohen's d")  + 
	scale_color_discrete(bquote(R^2)) + 
	geom_hline(yintercept=0.8, color="red", linetype="dashed") + 
	ylab("Power") +
	xlim(0, 1) +
	facet_grid(~Type)
```

Cohens $d = \frac{|\mu_1 - \mu_2|}{\sigma}$ is the effect size scaled by the within group standard deviation. Dashed line indicates 4000 cells

## Get effect size with 80% power
```{r tab3, results="asis", echo=FALSE}
res = data.table(res)
res$Dataset = with(res, paste(rsq, frac, Type))
# Sample size required to get 80% power
tab = res[,.SD[min(which(power>.80)),],by=Dataset]
# print(xtable(tab[,c('rsq', 'power', 'd')], type="html"), include.rownames=FALSE)
tab %>%
	select(Type, frac, d, rsq) %>%
	kable(type="html", include.rownames=FALSE)
```

# Power for xQTL

Consider $n$ samples where the response is measured with error so that the squared correlation between true and observed response is $R^2$.  Let a given SNP explain $f$% of the variance in the observed response.  Also note that if a SNP has a frequency $p$ and effect size $\beta$, the fraction of expression variation explained by the SNP is $2\beta^2 p(1-p)$  

```{r power, cache=FALSE}
n = 400
rsq = .8

getPower = function(n, rsq, f, n_tests){
	pwr.r.test(n*rsq, r=sqrt(f), sig.level=0.05/n_tests)
}

res = lapply(1:nrow(settings), function(i){
	n_tests = with(settings, nFeatures[i]*nSNPs[i]*n_cell_types[i])

	# for each f value
	lapply( seq(0, .151, length.out=500), function(f){
		# for each rsq
		lapply( c(.7, .8, .9, 1), function(rsq){
			res = getPower(n, rsq, f, n_tests)
			data.frame(Type = settings$Type[i], n, rsq, f, power=res$power)
		}) %>% 
		bind_rows
	}) %>% 
	bind_rows
}) %>% 
bind_rows

res$rsq_text = with(res, factor(rsq, rev(sort(unique(rsq)))))
res = res[order(res$rsq_text, decreasing=FALSE),]


# Sample size required to get 80% power
df_pwr_80 = res %>%
	filter(rsq == 0.8) %>%
	group_by(Type) %>%
	summarize(f = f[min(which(power>.80))]) %>%
	mutate(Type = factor(Type, settings$Type))


df_pwr_80 %>%
	ggplot(aes(f*100, Type, fill=Type, label=round(f*100, 1))) +
		geom_col() + 
		geom_text(hjust=-.2) +
		theme_bw(16) + 
		theme(aspect.ratio=1, plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="none") +
	xlab("Variance explained (%)") +
	ylab("Assay") +
	scale_x_continuous(lim=c(0, 16), expand=c(0,0))

res %>%
	mutate(Type = factor(Type, settings$Type)) %>%
	ggplot(aes(f*100, power, color=rsq_text)) + 
	geom_line(size=2) + 
	theme_bw(16) + 
	theme(aspect.ratio=1, plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5), legend.position="none") + 
	xlab("Variance explained (%)") + 
	scale_color_discrete(bquote(R^2)) + 
	geom_hline(yintercept=0.8, color="red", linetype="dashed") +
	geom_vline(aes(xintercept=f*100), data = df_pwr_80, color="blue", linetype="dashed") + 
	scale_x_continuous(expand=c(0,0)) + 
	scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,1), expand=c(0,0.01)) + 
	ylab("Power") +
	facet_wrap(~ Type)
```
